target_customer: B2C e-commerce merchants, from mid-market to established brands, mainly on Shopify
problem: E-commerce logistics (checkout delivery options, tracking, returns, refunds) is fragmented across carriers and tools and handled manually. Pango uses natural-language-built agents to automate it.
business_model: B2B SaaS for e-commerce logistics (delivery management, returns, tracking, TMS) with AI agents

founders.name: Steve Rahimi
founders.background_notes: YC page says e-commerce entrepreneur since age 17 with seven years building and scaling in e-commerce and tech.

founders.name: Lukasz Reszczynski
education: Liverpool John Moores University, MSc Astrophysics
Universitat Wien, PhD Molecular Biology (dropped out)
founders.background_notes: Built a patented configurator behind $1.5B in quotes; acting CTO for several companies. Source: YC company page.

competitors.name: Loop Returns
competitors.traction_then: about 4.7 of 5 on G2 across 62 reviews

competitors.name: Narvar
competitors.what: Post-purchase tracking and returns for larger retailers
competitors.traction_then: pricing roughly 30,000 to 45,000 USD per year per a vendor comparison

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating 100+ carriers, warehouses and storefronts is standard but laborious engineering; the agent layer adds moderate difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Integration breadth and embedded workflows create some lock-in, but mature competitors already offer similar returns and tracking and the agent layer is copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established vendors already sell the same wedge; no response specific to Pango found yet.

market_need_then: Merchants juggle many carriers and manual returns work. The company claims 30 brands signed and 99% of returns and shipping operations automated, which are self-reported figures.

brand_strength.rationale: No press on the brand found; the name Pango is shared by other companies, some using a pangolin mascot.

outcome_analysis: Pango is an active Summer 2026 YC company with no outcome yet. It spent 12 months embedded with 30 e-commerce brands before launching, which suggests early pull, but the market has entrenched returns vendors and only self-reported metrics exist. No verified funding was found.
notes: Only funding figure is a $500K angel round on a single aggregator profile (yespress.io); unverified and not recorded as a round. One source places the company in Stockholm while YC lists New York City. No shutdown or acquisition found.
